card.title: Choose What Matters More
card.instruction: Make someone choose between emotional safety and the outcome they claim to want.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They're calling your audition number. Do you want the part enough to let them hear you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want it. I don't want them laughing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can walk you in or drive you home. Which want am I helping?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Walk me in, but promise they won't laugh.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can promise I'll stay. Is that enough to risk the audition, or are we going home?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 audition opportunity asks risk, A3 separates walking in from going home and A5 offers support without guaranteeing immunity from laughter.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 fear shapes A3 explicit alternatives; B4 no-laughter condition causes A5 realistic staying promise and renewed choice.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the role and fears humiliation; B4 asks for reassurance that A cannot honestly provide.

heightening.evidence: B4 impossible safety condition makes A5 distinguish support from guaranteed outcome, sharpening the actual choice.

specificity.evidence: A1 called number and B2 desired part establish an immediate audition decision.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 staying versus going home makes the emotional trade-off concrete without belittling fear.
